summary: Production code imports a project module outside `python.sourceRoots`.
why: Code outside the source roots is not checked by the gate, so production code must not depend on it.
allowed: Move the imported code under a source root, or add its folder to `python.sourceRoots` so the gate checks it.

summary: A module that is in an import cycle with other modules of its package.
why: A cycle makes modules impossible to load, test or replace one at a time.
allowed: Move what they share into a module both import, or pass it in instead of importing it back.

summary: A package that is in a dependency cycle with other packages.
why: A cycle makes packages impossible to load, test or replace one at a time.
allowed: Move the shared types down into one of them, or invert one dependency behind an interface.

why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Use the real type, a `Protocol`, a `TypeVar` or a frozen dataclass; parse untrusted data at the boundary so the domain only sees typed values.

summary: `<name>` ignores every error
why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Name the expected exception: `contextlib.suppress(KeyError)`; or handle it or re-raise it with its cause. In a test, use `pytest.raises(SpecificError)` (`self.assertRaises` in unittest).

summary: `<name>` logs a caught error without its traceback
why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Keep the traceback: `logger.exception("message")` or `logger.error("message", exc_info=True)`; the exception as an argument drops it. Re-raising after the log also passes.

why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Take the time as a parameter or a `Callable[[], datetime]` and call `datetime.now(tz=UTC)` in the composition root.

why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Read the credential from the environment in the composition root and pass it in; never commit a key, token, private key or URL with a password.

why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Declare an enum: `class Status(enum.StrEnum): ACTIVE = "active"` on Python 3.11+, otherwise `class Status(str, enum.Enum)`.

why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Declare records as `@dataclass(frozen=True)` and build a changed copy with `dataclasses.replace`.

why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Name it for its job (`price_rounding.py`, `OrderRepository`); shared logic that belongs to no feature lives in `shared/` under a name that says what it does.

why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Parse untrusted input once at the boundary with pydantic (`Model.model_validate(data)`) in an `adapters/` package, not with `isinstance` checks or a `TypeGuard`.

why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Read the secret from the environment in the composition root (`os.environ["API_TOKEN"]`) and pass it in; keep placeholders such as `"changeme"` out of production code.

why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Pass a timeout in seconds: `urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=10)`, `session.get(url, timeout=10)`, or set `socket.setdefaulttimeout(10)` once at startup for `urllib`; an `httpx` client keeps its 5 second default unless you pass another number (`httpx.Client(timeout=10)`), never `timeout=None`.

why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.

allowed: Batch it: fetch or write all items in one call, or run the calls together with `asyncio.gather` or a `ThreadPoolExecutor.map` when there is no batch API.

why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Keep the state in an object that is created in the composition root and passed in, or build a new immutable value and return it. A registry filled once at import time (a decorator that adds the function to a table) is not run-time state; the exception route below covers its path.

summary: `<name>` reaches the network in a unit test
why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Replace the network with a fake: patch the client with `monkeypatch`, use `responses` or `respx`, or move the test to an `integration/` folder.

allowed: Read the environment once in the composition root (`main.py`, `settings.py`, a `composition_root/` package) and pass the values in as arguments or a frozen settings dataclass.

why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.

summary: `<name>()` reads the real clock in a test
why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Freeze or inject the time: pass a fixed `datetime` in, use `freezegun` or `time_machine`, or patch the clock with `monkeypatch`.

allowed: Run the program directly with the arguments as a list and leave the shell out: `subprocess.run(["git", "status"], check=True)`; `shell=False` is the default.

why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Control the clock instead of waiting: inject a fake clock, patch `time.sleep` with `monkeypatch`, or poll a condition with a bounded retry helper.

summary: `<name>` runs a query built by formatting a string
why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Pass the values as query parameters: `cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s", (user_id,))`, `session.execute(text("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = :id"), {"id": user_id})` in SQLAlchemy, `Model.objects.raw("... WHERE id = %s", [user_id])` in Django. Build placeholder lists from placeholders alone (`", ".join(["%s"] * len(ids))`) and optional filters as `conditions.append("name = %s")` joined with `" AND "`. A table or column name comes from a fixed lookup (`COLUMNS[key]` over a dict of constant names), a check against a constant set that stops otherwise (`if column not in ALLOWED: raise ValueError(column)`), a `Literal[...]` or `Enum` value, the schema (`table.name`, `model._meta.db_table`), or a quoting call (`psycopg.sql.Identifier(name)`, `dialect.identifier_preparer.quote(name)`).

summary: `<name>` sits beside its source and replaces it for the checkers
why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Delete the `.pyi` file and annotate the `.py` file itself.

summary: `<name>` swallows the error: it only logs it or returns a default, and carries on
why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Re-raise it with its cause (`raise DomainError(...) from error`), return a failure result that carries the error (`return Rejected(str(error))`), or collect it for the caller (`errors.append(error)`); logging alone is not handling. `contextlib.suppress(SpecificError)` ignores one expected error. In a test, use `pytest.raises(SpecificError)` (`self.assertRaises` in unittest).

why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Assert on the result of the code under test: `assert total(order) == Decimal("12.50")`.

allowed: Move test helpers and fixtures into the tests folder (`tests/support/`, `conftest.py`) so they do not ship with the package. A library's public `testing` module is allowed when the package `__init__.py` imports it or lists it in `__all__`.

summary: Test `<name>` has no assertion
why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Assert the outcome: `assert result == expected`, `with pytest.raises(SomeError):`, or call one of the assertion helpers the project tests use.

summary: `<name>` turns off TLS certificate verification, or lets the environment turn it off
why: One of the checks of nitpicker's own Python script. It runs on the Python source and tests and names one allowed form.
allowed: Keep verification on in every environment and trust the certificate authority instead: `requests.get(url, verify="/etc/ssl/private-ca.pem", timeout=10)`, `ssl.create_default_context(cafile=ca_path)`, `tlsCAFile=ca_path` for MongoDB, or `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` and `SSL_CERT_FILE` pointing at the bundle. A server that asks for optional client certificates uses `ssl.create_default_context(ssl.Purpose.CLIENT_AUTH)` with `verify_mode = ssl.CERT_OPTIONAL`; a server context that loads its own certificate needs no `verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE` line: delete it.
